answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making each identity costly to create: every agent must lock a refundable stake before it can transact, like a raven guarding its nest. A flood of fake agents then faces real expense, the tundra of free identities becomes a priced frontier, and each duplicate burns capital instead of earning it. Honest agents recover their stake through good work, while the saffron lure of cheap fake volume fades because ten thousand fake identities cost ten thousand stakes.
